A secret technique bestowed by the Purification Sisters.
It is said that as long as this blessing is active, one will not bear demon spawn. However, the tale of a defeated holy sister giving birth to a monster suggests the possibility of a demonic technique that can negate the blessing.

Buried remains of shattered corpses and fallen undead, reawakened beneath the earth.
When the living draw near, countless hands emerge, dragging victims into the grave.
Those taken are devoured—becoming yet another grasping hand in the abyss.

A crucified person who has turned into a zombie, or perhaps a zombie that was crucified to prevent it from moving.
Using projectile stomach acid, it greatly damages clothing.

A revived corpse that had been buried in a coffin.
Even after defeat, it can be reanimated through necromancy again and again.

A forsaken Gravekeeper versed in forbidden rites to raise the dead.
Born with skeletal deformities and a broken voice, he was shunned and forced into his role.
His prayers, warped by heresy, now grant him crude dominion over the undead.

Relatively small Enenuth with short tentacles are referred to as Mini Enenuth.
They don't pose much threat in small numbers, but enough of them can manage to knock a human down.
Humans who have been knocked down will have all of their magic sucked out by the Enenuth.

An enormous Enenuth that births other Enenuths.
After weakening victims using tentacles spread across the ground, it offers them as sustenance to the offspring it produces.

Demihumans of this size generally move in groups and prefer ganging up to torment other creatures.
Though lacking in physical and magical power, they make use of their small bodies to launch surprise attacks.

When a fleshy lump of Livor gets a taste for flesh and blood, it equips itself with a large mouth to eat people.
Although this demon's mouth has plenty of power to lift and hold its prey, it doesn't possess any weapons to kill living creatures right away.
A human unable to escape being fed upon by a Bobel will remain conscious until they're completely digested.

A swamp fly grotesquely transformed through an Abomination Broodling's influence.
Has the appearance of lumps of flesh attempting to replicate a fly's body shape.
It attempts to assimilate its prey's body into itself.

A large leech that lurks in the swamp.
It quickly stakes its claim on prey that falls into its territory by swallowing it whole, slowly stealing bodily fluids and magic power while it's inside.

A gathering of mature leeches mimicking the form of a human.
It makes use of the leeches' ability to contract and expand with its attacks, but the way it tries to lay eggs in a captured human is closer to human mating.

Leech spawned by the swamp's Abomination Broodling.
They quietly move throughout the swamp, quickly latching on when they get close to prey, sucking out bodily fluids and magic power.
They group up like beasts, the hidden leeches coming out when they think their prey is weak to attack together.

A monstrous leech bearing eggs and very small leeches within its body.
It can barely move with its enlarged body, but it can vomit up small leeches to attack, and will attempt to pin prey down to implant leech eggs within its body.

Years ago, a limbless, blood-craving infant was cast into the swamp as an Abomination Broodling.
The leeches swarmed it, but instead of being devoured, the child consumed them—mutating and growing at an unnatural rate.
Now, the swamp writhes with monstrous leeches, a cursed land born from that forsaken brood.

Once a treacherous marsh, now twisted further by the burrowing of giant leeches. Their relentless tunneling has reshaped the land into an unpredictable mire.
The murky waters obscure the depths, hiding patches of sinking sludge—soft and deep enough to swallow a person whole.

Newly hatched baby leeches.
Small enough to go unnoticed, they quietly latch on, feeding on blood and magic until they grow.

Babies born with the Abomination Broodling's Curse have demonic characteristics.
Their properties differ between cases, but many Abomination Broodlings share an ability to warp and distort living creatures in their surroundings by interfering with their magic.
This baby has fused with a nun, chaotically multiplying and breeding.

Monsters resembling humans that live in human-like communities.
Cruel by nature, they revel in plundering people and property.
In battle, they use tools and cunning tactics, such as kicking up sand to blind their foes.
Use the key at the entrance to the cathedral.

Particularly large-bodied demihumans, with the strength to lift a person with one hand.
They're slow and lack the cunning to strategize, but their grasp is hard to break free from, even with purification powers.
Additionally, there are some who wield huge weapons using their strong bodies.
Obtain a lead on the cathedral and its priests.

Legends of demihumans have existed since ancient times, but unlike today's marauders, they were said never to appear in human settlements.
It is believed they became monsters some time after a one particular ferocious infant with multiple faces and genitalia was born in town.

A cathedral priest that effectively rules over the Northeast Village via parasites.
Believes that the Otherworlder's appearance brings truth and salvation.
The arms growing from his head are used for defense and restraining opponents, and those caught will have parasites implanted.

Parasitized by monsters that alter human consciousness.
The progression of the parasitism is still suppressed by purification power.
Spread the sacred vessels and breed as much as possible.

One of the parasitized villagers.
At first glance, he appears to live a normal life, but when he perceives an outsider entering the village, he suddenly swings a bladed tool in a stiff, unnatural manner.

One of the parasitized villagers.
Though the parasite has altered his mind, much of his original memory and knowledge remain, allowing him to strike precisely at vital points.

Demihumans wearing stone masks adorned with distinctive patterns. 
The masks carry ritualistic significance and offer some protection against attacks.
Also, these demihumans tend to be more belligerent and bloodthirsty.

One of the parasitized villagers.
Armed with a farming scythe, she aims for the necks of intruders.
The parasite has altered her mind, leaving no restraint to protect her own body, allowing her to strike with strength far beyond that of an average woman.

A further-mutated parasitized villager, driven berserk.
The parasite has overtaken his body, growing large enough to latch onto walls and ceilings. With all control lost, he now exists only to capture prey and implant parasite eggs.

The demihumans imprison captured human women as breeding stock.
It is thought that their animalistic sides seek to procreate, while their human sides also seek pleasure.
It is also possible that this behavior began as a kind of ritual to summon their deity.

A further stage of parasitism in villagers.
The hole in his face reveals part of a mature parasite.
Besides functioning similarly to insect antennae, they can fly out to seek and attack new hosts.

A further mutated parasitized villager.
Swarming parasites writhe across her face, ready to leap onto new hosts at the first sight of prey.
Large demihumans donning masks hold higher positions, behaving like leaders who command other demihumans.

Originally a human rapidly grown by the parasite, its body is now unrecognizable.
Though sluggish overall, it exhibits sudden bursts of agility when using parasites to ensnare prey.

A flesh puppet infused with parasites, born from an experiment to create a vessel for the Otherworlder.
The parasites harbor faint traces of their essence, and like a holy relic, are believed to channel their otherworldly blessings.

A particularly aggressive and influential group among the demihumans.
While out hunting and raiding, they returned to find their home in ruins. Tracking the scent they left on the women, they arrived at the village.
They force their underlings to push carts stolen from humans, using them as makeshift war machines.

Hidden among the Imitation Offspring is the master of the parasites, the "Priest's Abomination Broodling."
Born through ritualistic mating to spread devotion to the Otherworlder, this creature alters minds by sharing its own flesh and blood, forcibly instilling faith.
The priest directs it toward two main purposes—eliminating external threats and preparing vessels for the Otherworlder.
They appear after Abomination Broodlings found in various locales have been purged.

As the distortion progresses, a larger, more grotesque form emerges.
Layered masses of flesh block arrows entirely, and if the core is hidden behind them, it cannot be destroyed.
Additionally, if the core splits into multiple pieces, all must be destroyed at once to prevent regeneration.
Can be seen in various locations.

One of the cathedral priests who worship the Otherworlder. 
The human staff uses attack magic rooted in blood from its flesh puppet.
Though not powerful in battle, they use curses to manipulate people's minds.

One of the cathedral priests who worships the Otherworlder. 
The cage staff forms magical hands made of blood to ensnare and defile prey.
Plans on capturing [[PlayerName]] alive, to make her a brood mother for the Otherworlder.

Mutated nun with oversized eyes.
Anyone exposed to the light of her gaze falls under mind control, drawing them defenselessly toward her.
She then feeds them sweet magic energy mouth to mouth, and those who ingest it waste away.

Status effect that forces drowsiness.
If left in this state, consciousness may slip away entirely.

Cursed traps that attack invaders.
Their movements are limited, but they make up for that in number.

A cursed trap hidden among piles of treasure.
After stealing its target's magic, it gradually turns their body to gold, adding the invader to the treasure room.

When faith in the Otherworlder overtook the cathedral, the sacred remains that once rested within were defiled and fed to pigs.
Still, traces of their power as miracle conduits remained. Through consumption, the pigs became vessels for the Otherworlder's so-called 'miracles.'

A huge cursed painting that reigns as master of the treasure room.
Within the painting lurks an eyeball monster, which extends tentacles to drag victims inside the canvas.
People dragged inside become portraits of defeat.

Fleshy masses hanging from ceilings equipped with gaping mouths meant to devour humans.
They dangle long, sensitive tongues down to detect approaching creatures, then draw captured prey into their maws.
Their sensitive tongues recoil upon taking damage.

A condition where magic has slowed physical movement.
This magic was developed in an attempt to approach the Otherworlder's command over space and time, but is imperfect.
Wears off over time.

In their pursuit of the Otherworlder, these priests took on a twisted form—eldritch beings that exude a mist slowing the movements of creatures and feed on human brains.
Though unstable and nearly invisible, their presence distorts nearby flames, making unnaturally flickering lights a telltale sign of their lurking presence.

A priest who worked in bookbinding.
Uses a large scythe to flay humans, making books with their skin.

A mass of fused Brain Snails.
Even after descending into monstrosity, they desperately struggle to merge into a single, greater entity.
Their immense magical power renders direct magic attacks ineffective.
They attack with projectile magic, and those who gaze into the light from their brain-eyes risk having foreign knowledge forced into them, twisting their minds into something inhuman.

Powder that lets you see things not of this world.

A device set up by the Gravekeeper to create zombies.

Seeds that take root even within human hosts, eventually transforming them into plants.

A bigger slug.

A being that exists between the mind and body of a pregnant woman, forming the origin of an Abomination Broodling.
When sperm reaches its destined place and merges with the mother’s blood, a formless wickedness from beyond this world seeps in.
This intrusion congeals, eventually taking shape as an Abomination Broodling.

The state of being covered in slime that impairs mobility.

A parasitized livestock pig.
As the parasite jumps out upon defeat, it is possible that the pig is not a fully compatible host.

Master of the barnhouse, a pig-headed man who commands the pigs.
He sees humans as nothing more than livestock or feed, offering captured victims to his swine.
Women, however, are used for breeding.
Those who endure his pigs may undergo mutations, as livestock parasites reshape their bodies for reproduction.

Vision distorted from exposure to monster pollen.

Originally infesting animals, they now reside within humans.
While they do not fully take control of the body, parasitic growth causes unusual changes in certain parts of the body.

The breasts have grown abnormally large.
They're so heavy it makes movement difficult.

After conception, the Abomination Broodling rapidly grew within [[PlayerName]]'s womb.

An organ that has evolved to keep swallowed prey from being regurgitated.
Its creeping flesh walls and slender tentacles gradually ensnare its victims.

A cylindrical organ that hides in holes, capturing prey with its mouth-like part.
Those swallowed are then carried deeper into the Innards Cave.
It has a simple internal composition that's connected to the ground, making it impossible to completely defeat.
It can also jump out above ground to capture prey from outside.

Long, slender tentacles lurking in the ceiling.
Advanced nutrient-absorbing organs seize living creatures and drain their magical energy.

A defender of the inside of the body, tasked with attacking foreign intrusions.
Numerous and relentless, they emerge endlessly from various outlets.

A cluster of tentacles concentrated in certain areas within the creature.
Some secrete mucus to immobilize foes, others coil around prey with their long bodies, and some lash out like whips. Unless completely eradicated, they will regenerate.

Intestinal creatures spawned within the body.
Though fused to the flesh of the floors and walls, they move independently to swallow prey.
A developed head allows them to sense distant targets but also becomes their vulnerable weak point.

An organ that secretes slime inside the creature.
Launches slime projectiles toward intruders to slow down their movements.

An organ for capturing food within the body, moving like a descending ceiling.
A thick, flexible flesh wall and slender tentacles encircle and ensnare their prey.

Formerly human females, unfortunate enough to be taken from outside.
Fused with the scattered reproductive organs inside the monster, they are continually filled with clusters of eggs—too far gone to be saved.
When fresh nutrients approach, larvae hatch from the eggs in their abdomen and spring forth.

A newborn tentacle hatched from an egg cluster.
It seeks out magical essence, latching on like a leech. Its writhing, erratic movements make it difficult to predict.
While lacking the strength to overpower humans, its relentless actions can sometimes lead to prolonged suffering.

Tentacles hidden within accumulated mucus.
Their movement through the liquid makes them hard to track.
Those captured and unable to break free are dragged deeper into the mucus.

<size=18>[ Dungeon recollection ]</size>
When entering a cleared dungeon once more, you can start from your chosen area.

<size=18>[ Arrow Magic aiming ]</size>
When using arrow magic, holding Up or Down when readying an arrow makes targeting begin in that direction.

<size=18>[ Defilement ]</size>
Defilement" is a status effect that makes
it harder to escape from being restrained.
It accumulates when restrained by enemies.
Defilement can be purified at save points.

<size=18>[ Sword Magic properties ]</size>
Sword Magic can attack multiple enemies at once.
Also, it can do major damage to long, slender enemies and clustered enemies.

<size=18>[ Gallery and Hints ]</size>
Select unrevealed items in the gallery to display hints about how to unlock them.

<size=18>[ Unlocking Gallery ]</size>
Fighting an enemy will unlock items related to that enemy,
or events will be unlocked by viewing the event.
Also, once you clear a dungeon, all of the enemies and events associated with it will be unlocked.

<size=18>[ Boss rematches ]</size>
You can rematch a boss you have already defeated.
The boss will not drop Relics in a rematch.
